chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ibrāhīm, from Yūnus, from Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam, concerning...

The hadith of Bureyh: when he came with him to Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), he met Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar (عليه السلام). Hishām related the account to him, and when he finished, Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) said to Bureyh: “O Bureyh, how is your knowledge of your Book?” He said, “I am knowledgeable of it.” Then he said, “How confident are you in its interpretation?” He said, “None is more confident than I am in my knowledge of it.”

He said: Then Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) began reciting the Injīl. Bureyh said, “You are the one I have been seeking for fifty years, or one like you.” He said: So Bureyh believed, and his faith became excellent, and the woman who was with him also believed. Then Hishām, Bureyh, and the woman entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), and Hishām related to him the conversation that had occurred between Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā (عليه السلام) and Bureyh.
So Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said: “Offspring, some of them from others, and Allah is Hearing, Knowing.”

Then Bureyh said, “How do you have the Tawrāh, the Injīl, and the books of the Prophets?” He said, “They are with us as an inheritance from them. We recite them as they recited them, and we speak them as they spoke them. Indeed, Allah does not place a ḥujjah in His earth who is asked about something and says: ‘I do not know.’”

key_terms.آمَنَ: he believed, indicating Bureyh’s acceptance of faith
key_terms.الْإِنْجِيلَ: the Evangel, recited here by the Imam as a sign of inherited scriptural knowledge
key_terms.تَأْوِيلِهِ: its interpretation, meaning the deeper understanding of the scripture
key_terms.حُجَّةً: a divine proof or authority established by Allah on earth
key_terms.ذُرِّيَّةً: offspring or lineage, expressing inherited continuity
key_terms.وِرَاثَةً: as inheritance, referring to the transmission of sacred knowledge from the Prophets

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the Imams’ inherited knowledge of previous scriptures?
ai.summary: This narration describes Bureyh’s encounter with Imām Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), whose knowledge of the Injīl led Bureyh and the woman with him to faith. It emphasizes that the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام) inherit the revealed scriptures and possess authoritative knowledge, such that Allah’s ḥujjah on earth does not reply to questions with ignorance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Hassan Bin Ibrahim, from Yunus, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam,

‘In a Hadeeth of Bureyh, that when he went with him to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he met Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>. So Hisham related a story to him<sup>asws</sup>. So when he finished, Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said to Bureyh: ‘O Bureyh! How is your knowledge with your Book?’ He said, ‘I am a knower with it’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘How reliable are you with its interpretation?’ He said, ‘What I can rely in it with my knowledge’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> recited the Evangel. So Bureyh said, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> are the one I have been seeking since fifty years, or someone like you<sup>asws</sup>!’ So, Bureyh professed belief, and his belief was good, and the woman who was with him (also) expressed belief. So Hisham, and Bureyh and the woman went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and Hisham related to him<sup>asws</sup> the speech which flowed between Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> and Bureyh.
So Abu Abdullahasws said ‘[3:34] Offspring one from the other; and Allah is Hearing, Knowing’.

So Bureyh said, ‘Is there for you<sup>asws</sup>, the Torah, and the Evangel, and the Books of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘These are with us<sup>asws</sup> as an inheritance from them<sup>asws</sup>. We<sup>asws</sup> tend to recite these just as they<sup>as</sup> recited these, and we<sup>asws</sup> are saying it just as they<sup>as</sup> were saying it. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does not Make a Divine Authority to be in His<sup>azwj</sup> earth who is asked about something, so he<sup>asws</sup> would be saying: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> don’t know’’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Hassan ibn Ibrahim from Yunus from Hisham ibn al-Hakam about the narration of Burayh with whom he came to abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) but they met abu al-Hassan Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s.). Hisham explained to the Imams (a.s.) about Burayh. When he finished abu al-Hassan (a.s.) asked, “O Burayh, how is your knowledge of your book?” He rplied, “I know it.” The Imam (a.s.) then asked, “What is the degree of your confidence in its interpretation?” He said, “Not so muCh”???

The narrator has said, “Abu al-Hassan then begun to read (from) the Gospel. Burayh then said, “It is you whom I was searching for fifty years or someone like you.” He has said that Burayh accepted the faith and also the lady who was with him.” Burayh and Hisham and the lady then came to abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.). Hisham informed the Imam (a.s.) about what had happene between Burayh and abu al-Hassan (a.s.).
Abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) then said, “The generations that are from each other and Allah hears and knows best.”
Burayh then asked, “How have possessed the Torah and the Gospel and the books if the prophets?”

The Imam (a.s.) said, “ We receive them as in the form of inheritance from them. We read them as they would read them and speak about them as the prophets would do. Allah does grant Divine authority on His earth to those who if questioned would be able to give the right answer and say I do not know.”
